title: APO Duck Cutlets with Sour Cherry-Thyme Gravy
description: Lean duck breast cutlets cook gently in steam and are sliced into a smooth cherry and thyme gravy.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe, bottom drip pan and middle wire rack

ingredients.name: skinless boneless duck breast
ingredients.note: Weigh after removing skin, fat and silver skin; butterfly thick pieces.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water without a vegetable seasoning blend.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Fill the water tank and install the bottom drip pan. Preheat to 175°F with sous vide mode on, 100% steam, rear element on, top and bottom elements off. Set the food probe target to 165°F.

steps.title: Thin the breast meat
steps.text: Flatten {duck} between sheets of parchment to a uniform 1/2 inch, using the flat face of a meat mallet.

steps.title: Place the probe
steps.text: Set the cutlets unbagged in the pan on the middle rack. Insert the probe sideways to the center of the thickest piece. Begin cooking immediately and set a separate 15-minute reminder for the first temperature check; respond sooner if the probe signals.

steps.title: Infuse the thyme
steps.text: While the duck steams, simmer {broth}, {thyme} and {pepper} together in the HexClad, covered, for 5 minutes. Lift out the herb sprigs.

steps.title: Melt the cherries
steps.text: Stir {cherry} into the hot broth until it dissolves.

steps.title: Make the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and keep it bubbling gently for 1 minute, until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Steam the duck
steps.text: Cook for 18–38 minutes, checking from 15 minutes. Verify 165°F throughout each portion. Keep the cooked duck loosely covered in its juices.

steps.title: Slice and sauce
steps.text: Slice the duck very thinly across the grain and fold it through the warm cherry gravy. Spoon a generous layer of gravy over each portion.

notes: Make ahead: Trim and flatten the duck a day ahead, cover and refrigerate. Option A uses tart cherry. For gentler Option B, use smooth pear puree instead and leave the pepper for the table. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze thin slices under the cherry gravy for up to 6 weeks; duck breast gets firmer with a second heating. Fridge reheat: Place one portion and its sauce in a shallow covered dish. Install the APO bottom drip pan and preheat to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Insert the probe in the coldest center and set it to 165°F. Start checking after 12 minutes and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw a single portion in the refrigerator overnight, then use the fridge reheating method. Stir the sauce until smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 251 kcal, 27.0 g protein, 15.0 g total carbohydrate, 8.5 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 128 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
